name: lance_file::versions::v1::encoding::write_schema_dictionaries
behavior: write_schema_dictionaries mutably borrows writer and schema. It computes maximum field ID once, defaults to-1, then iterates every integer0..=max, looks up a mutable field and skips holes or nondictionary types. Runtime work depends on ID span, not only field count; negative-only/empty schemas iterate nothing. Field data_type conversion uses the core schema contract and may panic for malformed logical metadata. For a dictionary field, absent dictionary metadata is IO error naming field; absent in-memory values is InvalidInput naming field. Existing dictionary values are borrowed, not removed. Checks occur per field during traversal, so a later field failure does not undo earlier writes or schema mutations. Choose encoder using actual values.data_type(): is_numeric -> PlainEncoder, otherwise is_binary_like -> BinaryEncoder, otherwise Schema error. Await encode on a one-array slice; after success store returned position and values.len in dictionary offset/length. No local comparison to schema dictionary value type, flush/shutdown, rollback or all-fields preflight. Numeric write predicate is not the explicit eight-integer read whitelist; broad binary-like predicate includes views that read_binary_array rejects. Exact lower-codec support remains pending.
callers: V1 writer::write_footer and lance_table::io::manifest::write_manifest under V1 gate.
callees: Schema::max_field_id/mut_field_by_id; Field::data_type; numeric/binary predicates; PlainEncoder/BinaryEncoder::encode.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::encoding::populate_field_dictionary
behavior: Private async_recursion populate_field_dictionary branches on schema-declared DataType::Dictionary, requires metadata(IO error), and for binary-like values calls read_binary_array(nullable=true,stored offset/length,full range). Existing in-memory values do not bypass this load. IO can occur before later fields fail; helper holds mutable field state across await. Only Int8/16/32/64 and UInt8/16/32/64 dictionary value types enter fixed-stride loading with full range. Other nonbinary types produce Schema error with value_type, even though writer selection uses the broader numeric predicate. Binary view types enter the preceding branch but fail the four-type binary dispatcher as InvalidInput. No type fallback/migration is implemented. After successful load replace dict_info.values with Some(array). A dictionary node does not recurse into children; nondictionary nodes recursively process children in stored order. Error stops traversal after any prior successful mutations. async_recursion boxes recursive futures; no task is explicitly spawned, and no rollback or cancellation guard appears.
callers: populate_schema_dictionaries and recursive child traversal.
callees: Field::data_type; read_binary_array/read_fixed_stride_array; recursive self.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::format::metadata::Metadata::group_indices_to_batches
behavior: group_indices_to_batches documents sorted input but actually clones and sort_unstable sorts it. It scans increasing batch_id across cumulative ends and groups original absolute indices into an ordered BTreeMap, preserving duplicate values. Out-of-range IDs can advance to batch_id==num_batches and are retained there; no error is returned. A zero-length batch is skipped while its end<=index. Sorting changes caller ordering without a permutation result. The comment labels sort_unstable quick sort; that implementation claim is only a comment, not established by this file. Map iteration yields increasing batch IDs. Each group reads batch_offsets[batch_id] and subtracts that offset cast to u32, collecting BatchOffsets. Nonempty indices with entirely empty batch_offsets panic on this indexing; a nonempty sentinel vector permits a terminal pseudo-batch for out-of-file rows. Unsigned subtraction is unchecked on malformed offsets. An empty indices slice yields no groups. The observed V1 take consumer rejects batch_id>=num_batches later.
callers: V1 FileReader::take plus local test.
callees: num_batches; sort_unstable; BTreeMap grouping; vector offset subtraction.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::format::metadata::Metadata::range_to_batches
behavior: range_to_batches returns Result but first unwraps final offset, so empty metadata panics. Only range.end>last_as_usize is explicitly rejected as InvalidInput with range/bound. It casts start to i32 and binary-searches offsets, using insertion_point-1 on a miss. Unsorted/nonzero-first offsets, large casts and underflow are not checked; duplicate cumulative offsets permit binary_search to select any matching entry. It does not reject start>end. Iterate from chosen batch while below num_batches; stop once batch_start>=range.end. Append clamped(relative start..end) using unchecked usize subtraction, then return vector. Reversed ranges can yield reversed subranges; an empty range inside a nonempty batch can produce an empty subrange, while an empty range at its start stops immediately. The V1 reader short-circuits Range::is_empty before invoking this helper, so these helper-level observations are not claims that that caller exposes them.
callers: V1 FileReader::read_range after an empty-range guard, plus local test.
callees: binary_search; num_batches; min/max and relative range construction.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::page_table::PageTable::load
behavior: Public async load accepts borrowed reader, table position, signed inclusive min/max IDs and signed number of batches. Documentation requires caller dimensions and explains0/0 for absent/struct pages. Only max<min is explicitly rejected, as Internal with both values; negative IDs or num_batches are not rejected. Count inclusive field-ID range, compute ordinary usize length=num_columns*(num_batches as usize)*2, construct Int64 PlainDecoder and await decode, then unwrap Int64 downcast. Multiplication/casts, decoded length and values are not independently checked here. Negative batch count can imply a huge requested length; concrete IO/decode failures are delegated. Whole raw table is decoded before map expansion. For every field in the inclusive range insert an inner map; for batch0..num_batches use signed idx=field_pos_as_i32*num_batches+batch and read pair at2idx,2idx+1. Convert each signed64 position/length to usize unchecked and insert, including0/0 holes. Map lookup unwrap follows local insertion; array indexing relies on decoded shape. Negative values are not rejected. num_batches0 returns nonempty outer maps with empty inner maps, a state the writer does not safely handle.
callers: V1 reader ordinary/stats page-table paths and local tests.
callees: PlainDecoder::new/decode; Arrow downcast/index access; BTreeMap insertion.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::page_table::PageTable::write
behavior: write documents dense placeholders. Reject completely empty outer map with InvalidInput source empty page table. Then reject supplied min_field_id>observed minimum with InvalidInput whose message uses field_id_offset. Take observed max and build inclusive[min,max]. Lower min is allowed to include ancestor/hole fields; all checks here precede writer.tell. Await writer.tell for start position, then find maximum batch key across all inner maps, unwrap it, and add1. Nonempty outer/all-empty inner maps panic at unwrap after tell; batch-ID max overflow and casts are unchecked. Int64Builder capacity is field_count*num_batches, although two values will be appended per cell, so it underestimates final element count. No dimensions are persisted in this method. Iterate field-major then batch0..num_batches. Existing PageInfo appends position and length cast to i64; missing pair appends[0,0]. Finish Int64Array and write_all its first Arrow buffer directly, then return prior tell position. No explicit endian conversion, alignment, length prefix, footer, flush/shutdown or atomic/abort guard appears. A partial write/error/cancellation can leave output bytes; successful return is not publication/durability. A table whose only batch key is-1 derives0batches and writes an empty buffer; more negative/overflowed dimensions remain unchecked.
callers: V1 writer footer/stats page-table emission and local tests.
callees: Writer::tell; PageTable::get; Int64Builder; AsyncWriteExt::write_all.

callers: V1 writer null/fixed/binary/dictionary page setters, other pending writer branches and local tests.
